The original download is `f1_2026_concept_polygon_model.glb`. The adapted explorer asset is `qvist-2026-assemblies.glb`.

Changes for APEX: regrouped export chunks into 16 selectable display assemblies; subdivided triangles to make clean separation seams in fused bodywork; retained the original surface and silhouette; baked coordinate orientation; assigned red and graphite study finishes; removed redundant uniform vertex colors; normalized display size at runtime. The cuts are illustrative, not verified manufacturing joints. No complete internal engine or Ferrari SF-26 accuracy is claimed.

Keep this attribution, the source link, license link and changes notice with redistributed versions. No endorsement by the original creator, Ferrari, Formula One or the FIA is implied.

## Additional changes for APEX Gesture Lab, Build 003

The prepared 16-assembly derivative was obtained from
https://github.com/filan214/F1---2026-Car-Details/tree/main/dist/models
(preparation by filan214; original creator Qvist_designs).

Changes in this project: gzip packaging of the full-detail GLB; a separate convex-envelope silhouette LOD for software rendering; material adaptation, runtime display normalization, selection and illustrative explosion offsets. The simplified LOD deliberately loses cavities and small surface details and must not be used for engineering analysis. The full-detail asset retains the obtained prepared GLB geometry. Neither model is Red Bull CAD or a complete internal engine model. Attribution and model license apply independently of this project's MIT-licensed application code.

Build 004 additionally applies a neutral engineering material palette, hover highlights and optional x-ray/wireframe presentation. Source geometry is unchanged. The accompanying technical SVG schematics and notes are separate original educational illustrations, not recovered internals from the source model.
